summary: In this excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (labeled 'Book 11 — part 85'), Miranda and Jane are resting while Rebecca prepares the brick house for expected company, which includes returned missionaries from Syria. Rebecca works quickly to make the two south chambers neat and warm, and then the aunts come down to change clothes. Miranda is pleased by the results, and Rebecca also opens the parlor, arranging the room for the visitors, including Brother Milliken, who is coming to see Mr. Burch about business.
one_line: Rebecca readies the brick house's rooms and parlor for returned missionaries and guests while her aunts rest.
key_facts: Miranda tells Rebecca to fix up the two south chambers for the company.
Miranda says she will lie down beside Jane in their bedroom and must not be allowed to rest past five o'clock.
Miranda had baked a pot of beans in the middle of the week, which she says will come in handy.
Miranda says her father used to say nothing went right to the spot with returned missionaries like pork 'n' beans 'n' brown bread.
Rebecca dusts, pulls up shades, and sweeps floors with a whisk broom to prepare the brick house rooms.
When Rebecca calls her aunts at five o'clock, the beds are smooth, pitchers are filled, and soap and matches are laid out.
A large stick burns slowly in each air-tight stove in the upstairs rooms.
Rebecca says the company is right from Syria and that she must look it up in the geography.
The front parlor has a cheerful blaze in the open stove, and a fire is laid on the hearth in the back room.
Rebecca's rose-colored lamp, her second Christmas present from Mr. Aladdin, stands on a marble-topped table in the corner.
Miranda asks Rebecca whether they should open the parlor, and Rebecca says they did so on Thanksgiving and Christmas.
Rebecca moved the wax flowers off the mantelpiece so they would not melt.
Rebecca put the shells, the coral, and the green stuffed bird on top of the what-not so the children would not play with them.
Brother Milliken is coming over to see Mr. Burch about business.
